description:
FOUND s513 (Fable, 2026-10-09 03:5x) reviewing s513b (#2871 position-aware prototypes) -- probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s513/review/p513b/c1.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs main 3a925fa3 vs the s513b tree a8fcf0df (IDENTICAL on both trees: pre-existing, NOT a regression of the batch):
    no strict; no warnings; my $v1 = PI * 2; my $v2 = PI + 2; my $v3 = PI; use constant PI => 3; print "$v1 $v2 $v3\n";
    perl: 0 2 PI        PCL: 6 3 3
EMISSION (tree): (p-* (p-scalar-ctx (pl-PI)) 2) / (p-scalar-ctx (pl-PI 2)) / (pl-PI) -- the bareword above the `use constant` is lowered as a CALL of the constant sub (with `+ 2` as its ARGUMENT), so the positional rule #2871 built for the PROTOTYPE consumers is not reached: the bareword-is-call / is-known-callable classifier keeps WHOLE-FILE existence for a name a later `use constant` declares.  s513b's consumer table said a constant below answers 'not-yet' (a string) for `_bareword_callable_here`; this spelling goes through a different consumer (the term classifier that emits `(pl-NAME args)`), or the existence answer `file sub: callable (existence stays whole-file)` is applied to the constant's sub too.  The PRINT spelling (`print PI * 2; use constant PI => 3`, the review's p16) is a whole-statement DROP (#2920), which is why the batch's own probe did not see this one.
FIX SHAPE: the existence answer for a name declared by `use constant` (and by an IMPORT: `use M qw(f)` declares f at the `use`) must be positional like its prototype -- a call site above the declaring statement answers 'unknown' -> the bareword is a string (perl), not 'not-yet' + call.  A sub DEFINED later in the file stays callable above (perl: `f(1)` above `sub f` is a call; bare `f` above is a string under no strict -- probe both).  Guard rows in Pl/t/proto-position-01.t (the file s513b made): the three spellings above, inverse-verified.
POPULATION: corpus-diff was IDENTICAL for #2871 over 111 files, so the shape is rare in the corpora; it is the review's p16 shape (static-parse-limits-review-s512.md Â§3) in its non-print spelling.
subject: RESIDUE of #2871 (found by the s513b review probe): a `use constant` NAME used ABOVE its declaration in a non-print statement is still a CALL -- `my $v = PI * 2; use constant PI => 3;` gives 6 (perl 0: the bareword is the string "PI"), `PI + 2` emits `(pl-PI 2)` = 3 (perl 2)
